items.title: Universal XSS in uBlock Origin from website-driven element picker
items.summary: A critical vulnerability has been discovered in uBlock Origin that allows for universal cross-site scripting (XSS) through a flaw in its element picker feature. Developers and users of this popular ad-blocking extension should update immediately to mitigate potential security risks.

items.title: Qwen4-Max
items.summary: The release of Qwen4-Max introduces significant improvements in AI model performance, particularly in natural language processing tasks. This advancement is crucial for developers looking to leverage cutting-edge AI capabilities in their applications.

items.title: Protomaps: Self-hosting map tiles has gotten cheap and easy
items.summary: Protomaps has made self-hosting map tiles more accessible and affordable, allowing developers to integrate customizable maps into their applications without relying on third-party services. This shift empowers developers to maintain control over their mapping solutions.

items.title: Tor Project Issues Rapid-Response DoS-Defense Fix Amid Sustained DDoS Attack
items.summary: The Tor Project has released a critical update to address a sustained DDoS attack, enhancing its defenses against potential service disruptions. This update is vital for developers and users relying on Tor for secure communications.

items.title: Winudf – DVD / BluRay driver for DOS, Windows 1.x – 3x / 95 / 98 / ME
items.summary: The Winudf project has released an open-source driver that enables DVD and BluRay support for legacy Windows operating systems, including DOS and Windows 95/98. This development is significant for developers maintaining older systems or creating retro applications.
